`-RCDevVerticalAccept YES` (or `in-place`, which unticks Make a copy first),
with which the Make Vertical Version sheet presses its own Make once it is
first enabled (spec §11 VR-39 (h)); and `-RCDevDerivedHidden YES`, with which `new_project_from_range` opens its
document with no window (`display: false`), so a proof can see the windowless
door (spec §11 CJ-52); and `-RCDevExportFault audio@N|video@N|audio-hold@N`, the same for an
`ExportWriter` export's pumps, spec §11 #378), which
Distribution does not. `rc_op_names`
and the catalog are the authority for the counts; the parity check compares
them at startup. `render_frame` writes a PNG and returns its path; `export`
puts the job on the Export Queue and answers an `export_id` at once, and
`export_status` answers it until `done` (`mcp.py`'s `export_with` waits; spec
§11 #326).

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. An instance DEADLOCKS somewhere past forty documents open at once:
a proof that closes what it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and
one that does not relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. Its scale is
`-RCDevCaptureScale 1|2|3` (spec §11 #539), which `screens.py` pins to 2, so a
capture is 2× on a 1× display without moving a window. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Binding for every stage of the "fixes" batches (2026-11-09)

The owner, 2026-11-09: "Start fixing everything in 'Defects with a fix already named in the issue'. Use 3 lanes to fix issues in parallel. Try to batch issues where feasible. Use /litecode for implementation."

The issues are review nits and defects filed by earlier road maps. Each names its file, its failure and a fix, and on 2026-11-08 the code site each one names was found still present on main at a0bae333. The named fix is a lead, not an order: read the code, confirm the failure by a test, probe or MCP row, and build the fix that is right for the code as it stands. Read each issue with `gh issue view <N> --comments`.

Where an issue cites `docs/guide/…`, that guide is retired: the documentation site in `docs/site/` is where the behaviour is documented now (`docs/site/CLAUDE.md` is its rulebook). Where an issue cites a road map record in `designs/<name>.md`, it is archived under `archive/` and condensed in `designs/adr/`.

### Where to work

- **The integration worktree** is I = `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int`, branch `fixes-int`. It is kept equal to `main` between landings.
  - Only the integrator writes there. Everyone else reads it at most.
  - Never touch the main checkout `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob`. The integrator alone fast-forwards `main` to I. Never push.
  - Never touch another lane's worktree.
- **The implementer and every fixer run in a worktree of their own.** It is your current working directory when you start; the harness made it from `main`'s HEAD, which holds every batch landed so far.
  - Before building, CoW-copy I's caches so the build is not cold. Skip any that are absent:
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/build ./build`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/core/target ./core/target`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/graphic/target ./graphic/target`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/mcp-proxy/target ./mcp-proxy/target`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/agent/node_modules ./agent/node_modules`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/tools/proof/media ./tools/proof/media`
    - `cp -cR /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int/docs/site/node_modules ./docs/site/node_modules`
  - A fixer copies these from the previous stage's worktree instead; it is told which.
  - Use absolute paths inside your own worktree. Write a multi-step shell sequence to a script file in your scratch folder and run it as one command.
- The designer, adversary and reviewer read code in I (read-only).
- **Scratch files** go in a subfolder of the scratchpad named after your batch and stage, never its root. Three lanes share it.

### Owner questions

A decision in spec §11 is not re-litigated. A fix that needs a new decision, or amends one (several issues say "or amend AU-nn to say so"), records it in the newest suitable file in `designs/spec/11-decisions/` with its index row, BEFORE the code. Where an issue offers "fix the code OR record the limit", prefer fixing the code unless the fix is disproportionate; say which you chose and why. If a fix needs a genuine owner choice (a trade-off between behaviours the owner would notice, dropping something they asked for), do not choose:

- If it holds back only some issues, list them in the spec under `## Held for the owner`, each with the question, the options and your recommendation, and go on without them.
- Only if nothing in the batch can proceed, write `STOP: <the question, the options, your recommendation>` at the top of your output.

### Fixes

- **Each fix gets a check that is red without it and green with it.** A core change gets a test in `core/tests/`. An app change gets a probe row (through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`) or an MCP proof row in the area's existing proof in `tools/proof/`, not a throwaway. Then prove red: apply a mutant that restores the old behaviour at the fix's site, run the row, record that it fails, and revert the mutant. A row that was never seen red proves nothing. Record both results in `04-checks.txt`.
- A user-visible change follows the root CLAUDE.md's recipe: spec §5.2/§6/§7.9 for anything they mirror, and an MCP mirror for every user-visible edit. The parity check stays clean. A text the fix changes on the site (`docs/site/`) is updated with it, and `python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` run.
- A persisted field bumps `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` and the header, with a `schema_vN.rs`. None of this round's issues should need one; say so if one does.
- A check only a person can make is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, in the same change.
- **File size:** a file at ~600 lines gives something up before it takes anything on, by a pure move committed alone (`TranscriptTabSource.swift` at 598 and `AnalysisFrames.swift` at 409 are named by their issues). New files are capped at 400 lines. Frozen files take wiring only. Never run `xcodegen` bare; use `make project`.
- **Residue rule:** a problem the batch uncovers in code it is in is fixed in the batch. Only work that needs the owner, or is as big as the batch, goes under "To file" in your notes, with a draft title and body.
- **Never edit any CLAUDE.md.** List each edit needed under "CLAUDE.md edits owed", with the exact text. The integrator applies them. `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` included.

### Verification

Follows the root CLAUDE.md's "Verification" section.

- Targeted tests and probes in the loop. `make typecheck` after Swift edits: 0 errors and exactly the 4 baseline warnings. `make lint` and `cargo fmt` after Rust edits.
- `make app-debug` before driving the app. Launch your own instance with `python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch`, and stop only that pid. `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` must print nothing before you trust a run.
- Mutants for the decisions the batch adds (the red/green rule above covers each fix's own).
- `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete, in the foreground (Bash timeout 600000). Three lanes share the machine, so it can run past the 600 s cap; a re-run skips what already passed, so run it again rather than backgrounding it.
- Any MCP proof the batch adds rows to runs once against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`, after the gate's `make app`).
- Record each command and its result. A number in a record is written only when a run printed it.

### For the adversary and the reviewer

- **Adversary:** a fix planned without a red/green check is an objection; so is a plan that re-litigates a spec §11 decision, or that records a limit where a fix was cheap, or that fixes the issue's named line without reading whether the code around it has moved since the issue was filed.
- **Reviewer:** a fix with no row seen red is a blocker; so is a site page that still states the old behaviour, a parity complaint, or a fifth typecheck warning.

### Commits

The implementer and fixers COMMIT on their worktree's branch, naming paths explicitly, with a plain message. A pure move goes first in its own commit, with a subject starting `Pure move:`. Never commit `FrameJob.xcodeproj`, `tools/proof/work/`, `tools/proof/media/` or build products. Return the base sha (`main`'s HEAD when the worktree started), the tip sha and the worktree path. The integrator turns the range into one commit (pure moves excepted). A commit can take a few minutes to return: the repo's post-commit hook runs `entire`. Wait for it, and don't kill it.

### Things never to do

- **Never open, print, grep or list anything under `.secrets/`.** Never spend money: no `--live` proof, no paid call.
- **Never run Copy or Cut through the menu**, and never write to the general pasteboard.
- **Never perform a persisting menu item** on any build (View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality).
- **Never take the Mac's focus or put a window in front of the owner.** No `open`, no `osascript`, no System Events, no posted CGEvents.
- **Kill only a pid you launched.** The owner's own Frame Job, any other session's instance (`claude -w tutorial-handler` has one worktree under `.claude/worktrees/tutorial-handler`; leave it alone) and any dev server you didn't start are left alone.
- The Concat rule stands: none of its code, shaders, chains or colour tables.

- Only if nothing in the batch can proceed, write `STOP: <the question, the options, your recommendation>` at the top of your output.

### Fixes

- **Each fix gets a check that is red without it and green with it.** A core change gets a test in `core/tests/`. An app change gets a probe row (through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`) or an MCP proof row in the area's existing proof in `tools/proof/`, not a throwaway. Then prove red: apply a mutant that restores the old behaviour at the fix's site, run the row, record that it fails, and revert the mutant. A row that was never seen red proves nothing. Record both results in `04-checks.txt`.
- A user-visible change follows the root CLAUDE.md's recipe: spec §5.2/§6/§7.9 for anything they mirror, and an MCP mirror for every user-visible edit. The parity check stays clean. A text the fix changes on the site (`docs/site/`) is updated with it, and `python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` run.
- A persisted field bumps `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` and the header, with a `schema_vN.rs`. None of this round's issues should need one; say so if one does.
- A check only a person can make is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, in the same change.
- **File size:** a file at ~600 lines gives something up before it takes anything on, by a pure move committed alone (`TranscriptTabSource.swift` at 598 and `AnalysisFrames.swift` at 409 are named by their issues). New files are capped at 400 lines. Frozen files take wiring only. Never run `xcodegen` bare; use `make project`.
- **Residue rule:** a problem the batch uncovers in code it is in is fixed in the batch. Only work that needs the owner, or is as big as the batch, goes under "To file" in your notes, with a draft title and body.
- **Never edit any CLAUDE.md.** List each edit needed under "CLAUDE.md edits owed", with the exact text. The integrator applies them. `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` included.

### Verification

Follows the root CLAUDE.md's "Verification" section.

- Targeted tests and probes in the loop. `make typecheck` after Swift edits: 0 errors and exactly the 4 baseline warnings. `make lint` and `cargo fmt` after Rust edits.
- `make app-debug` before driving the app. Launch your own instance with `python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch`, and stop only that pid. `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` must print nothing before you trust a run.
- Mutants for the decisions the batch adds (the red/green rule above covers each fix's own).
- `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete, in the foreground (Bash timeout 600000). Three lanes share the machine, so it can run past the 600 s cap; a re-run skips what already passed, so run it again rather than backgrounding it.
- Any MCP proof the batch adds rows to runs once against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`, after the gate's `make app`).
- Record each command and its result. A number in a record is written only when a run printed it.

### For the adversary and the reviewer

- **Adversary:** a fix planned without a red/green check is an objection; so is a plan that re-litigates a spec §11 decision, or that records a limit where a fix was cheap, or that fixes the issue's named line without reading whether the code around it has moved since the issue was filed.
- **Reviewer:** a fix with no row seen red is a blocker; so is a site page that still states the old behaviour, a parity complaint, or a fifth typecheck warning.

### Commits

The implementer and fixers COMMIT on their worktree's branch, naming paths explicitly, with a plain message. A pure move goes first in its own commit, with a subject starting `Pure move:`. Never commit `FrameJob.xcodeproj`, `tools/proof/work/`, `tools/proof/media/` or build products. Return the base sha (`main`'s HEAD when the worktree started), the tip sha and the worktree path. The integrator turns the range into one commit (pure moves excepted). A commit can take a few minutes to return: the repo's post-commit hook runs `entire`. Wait for it, and don't kill it.

### Things never to do

- **Never open, print, grep or list anything under `.secrets/`.** Never spend money: no `--live` proof, no paid call.
- **Never run Copy or Cut through the menu**, and never write to the general pasteboard.
- **Never perform a persisting menu item** on any build (View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality).
- **Never take the Mac's focus or put a window in front of the owner.** No `open`, no `osascript`, no System Events, no posted CGEvents.
- **Kill only a pid you launched.** The owner's own Frame Job, any other session's instance (`claude -w tutorial-handler` has one worktree under `.claude/worktrees/tutorial-handler`; leave it alone) and any dev server you didn't start are left alone.
- The Concat rule stands: none of its code, shaders, chains or colour tables.

association:	owner
edited:	false
status:	none
--
Held for the owner; stays open. The batch (fixes b1, landed as commit ae0c9540 on main, not yet pushed) read the site: `same` in core/src/export_stems.rs still compares by `to_lowercase()` only, and the failure stands as described. No code was written for it because the fix needs a choice.

Question: how should the core compare stem names? Rust's std has no Unicode normalization, and nothing in core's Cargo.lock or the cargo registry provides it; the review that filed this advised against a dependency for its own sake.

Options:
1. Add the `unicode-normalization` crate to core (it brings `tinyvec` too). One network fetch at build; acknowledgements.py picks both up. `same` then compares `nfc().collect::<String>().to_lowercase()`, fixing both the grouping and the uniqueness check in about five changed lines.
2. Generate the canonical decomposition and combining-class tables into core/src from Python's `unicodedata`. No dependency, but two generated files of about 300 lines and a generator to keep.
3. Have Swift refuse the job when two stems' files fold equal under `precomposedStringWithCanonicalMapping` and a case-insensitive comparison. The names stay unfixed; the owner would see a refused export rather than a replaced file.
4. Record the limit in AU-108.

Recommendation: option 1 — the standard crate, the smallest change, and it fixes the grouping and the uniqueness check together.

--
     119 core/src/export_stems.rs
     400 core/tests/export_stems.rs
     519 total
core/Cargo.lock
[package]
name = "framejob-core"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "Apache-2.0"

[lib]
name = "framejob_core"
crate-type = ["staticlib", "rlib"]

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
# `preserve_order` is what `graphic` enables; a path dependency unifies it
# into this build anyway, so it is spelled here where a reader of the core
# will see it: `serde_json::Map` is insertion-ordered, and `recipe.rs`'s
# `content_hash` sorts before it hashes rather than lean on the map.
serde_json = { version = "1", features = ["preserve_order"] }
serde_path_to_error = "0.1.20"
tiny_http = "0.12"
# The CSS named-colour table `model_color.rs` reads (G-12): usvg 0.48.1's own
# pin, already in the lock through `graphic`, so a name the core stores is one
# the engine draws.
svgtypes = "0.16.1"
# The motion-graphics engine (road map 10, G-2): only `ffi_graphic.rs` names it.
graphic = { path = "../graphic" }
# The `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums (`graphic_package.rs`, G-46 (c)); also
# `graphic_ffi.rs`'s and `graphic_package.rs`'s test oracles. Already in the
# lock through `graphic`.
sha2 = "0.10"

[profile.release]
# No LTO: cargo skips it for a staticlib+rlib unit anyway, and asking for it
# fat-LTOs each of the 32 test binaries (designs/adr/rust-build-settings.md).
incremental = true

[patch.crates-io]
# graphic's vendored tiny-skia with the gradient dither (spec §11 PR-13): Cargo ignores the
# [patch] in graphic/Cargo.toml when building this crate, so it is restated here.
tiny-skia = { path = "../graphic/vendor/tiny-skia" }

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

content.content:
- **AU-107 — The plan labels its audio tracks.** Each `audio_tracks[]` entry is `{"id", "track",
  "segments", "ramps"}`: `track` (u32) is the id of the `Project::tracks` entry whose walk in
  `assign` placed it, so a nest's contents carry the nest clip's track. Written always; the plan
  is not persisted, so there is no format bump. Swift keeps the map composition track → timeline
  track per build (`BuiltComposition.audioOwners`), the family split by source format included:
  a composition track never carries two top-level timeline tracks (S3 Q1), so a selection by
  timeline track is a selection of whole composition tracks.
- **AU-108 — Stems (AU-101's).** (a) On the three audio rows only (`audio_m4a`, `audio_wav`,
  `audio_aiff`, whose presets list `stems: ["tracks", "names"]`); a movie row refuses (`<id> has
  no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff`), and a value but the two words
  is refused by name on any row. (b) `tracks`: one stem per heard timeline track; `names`: heard
  tracks whose trimmed names match case-insensitively are one stem, named by the first's
  spelling, and an unnamed track is its own. Heard = has a plan audio track labelled with it and
  is not `silenced` (mute, solo) among the timeline's tracks; none heard is refused (`stems: no
  track is heard, so there is no stem to write`). Order: timeline order of each stem's first
  track. (c) A name is the trimmed track name, else `Track N` (N = index + 1, the header's label),
  `/` and `:` replaced by `-`; a name equal case-insensitively to an earlier stem's gets
  ` (Track N)`, and one still equal to an earlier stem's ` (Track N, 2)`, ` (Track N, 3)` and on,
  the first no earlier stem holds, so no two stems share a file. The settings end with `stems: [{name, tracks}]` only when asked. (d) Files
  `<mix name without extension> - <name>.<mix extension>` beside the mix; an existing file at a
  stem's path is replaced without asking (the save panel asks only about the mix), except that a
  stem path naming one of the project's media files (symlinks resolved, case-insensitive) refuses
  the job before any stem file is touched, with `ExportStemsPipeline.SourceCollision`'s sentence
  (`The stem “<file name>” would replace media this project uses; export under another name.`);
  the guide says both. (e) **Pre-master:** a stem is its tracks' sub-mix exactly as the mix plays
  them (clips, envelope, ducks, track volume and pan, taps), with no loudness gain and no master
  limiter (`ExportAudioMaster(limits: false)`), rounded once at the job's depth and clipped only
  at full scale — so the stems sum to the mix within rounding wherever the master neither gains
  nor limits; the guide says so. (f) One job: the mix, then each stem in order, each from a fresh
  build of the same plan on the export's key (fresh taps, `ExporterLoudness.swift`'s reason)
  reading only its composition tracks, on one serial queue `com.kgalligan.framejob.export.stems`;
  progress is `(finished + current) / (1 + N)` of the write's share; a failure or a cancel leaves
  nothing (the pipeline removes the mix and each stem it finished); the line reads "Exported
  “Mix.wav” and 3 stems."; the `export_status` result lists each stem's `{name, tracks, path}`.
  (g) Not measured: the loudness report is the mix's.
4de064b8 The import probe's PQ read and first-frame decode and a converted strip's one-clip build run off the cooperative pool, and every AVAssetReader user is audited (fixes b3: #369)
13f408f2 Match Audio says a refusal once and smooths around a dropped band, Enhance Voice has one setup and enhance_voice one read hop, isolation fails on lanes that disagree, and a voiced clip's end no longer wants an isolation render (fixes a2: #410 #411 #412 #409 #397)
4076a513 A cancelled analysis job keeps what it decided, merging only into its own stamp's cache, and the analysis reader makes a frame's picture only when the kind asks (fixes b2: #435 #437)
50571291 A voice cache replaced under shown cloud words is read again at once, Remove Background's shut header follows a progress tick, a nil analysis stamp is never memoised, and analyze_cutout re-reads only the clips still analysing (fixes c2: #444 #438)
3bbbdd8d Switch by Speaker's empty range and crossed marker ranges, its argument errors before the plan, Make Vertical's failed save cleaned up, the recorder's follow-ups in the landing's container, and a vanished cache file skipped by the derived carry (fixes c1: #456 #457 #460 #458 #459)
448640ef A ⌥-press in a clip's last partial frame adds a volume point, an EQ with no slot on reads "off", Normalize's tooltip follows the mode in every window, Enhance's keep rule reads the clip's own limiter, and the loudness memos are keyed per document and without automation (fixes a1: #392 #407 #406 #400 #401 #413)
ae0c9540 Auto Zoom reads a cut's aim only from the hold spanning it, off refuses audio.eq beside a slot, the speech duck samples every crossing, and stems with no plan fail the export (fixes b1: #447 #398 #386 #394 #393)
057d80f0 A nest clip takes a crop but no corner radius or chroma key, and a camera layout writes a nest role's radius as 0 (ai-docs r3: #536 #535)

commit 448640eff6f5cd37a204a3238447a31737675b0b
Author: Kevin Galligan <kgalligan@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Nov 9 10:26:03 2026 -0500

    A ⌥-press in a clip's last partial frame adds a volume point, an EQ with no slot on reads "off", Normalize's tooltip follows the mode in every window, Enhance's keep rule reads the clip's own limiter, and the loudness memos are keyed per document and without automation (fixes a1: #392 #407 #406 #400 #401 #413)
    
    #392  VolumeLine.point guards on the raw press (0 ≤ clipTime < duration) and holds
          the snapped t to the start of the clip's last frame, so a press in a last
          partial frame adds its point there instead of beeping. Spec §11 AU-83 amended.
    #407  AudioPane.eqSummary reads "off" for no EQ or one with no slot on, bypassed or
          not; "bypassed"; else "N on". The EQ section's header calls it. Spec §11 AU-38
          amended; the site's audio/eq page says so.
    #406  NormalizeChoice posts didChangeNotification from both setters; AudioPane
          observes it, re-titles its Normalize button's tooltip and refreshes its
          inspector, so another window's pane follows a mode change at once. The Mode and
          Target write closures only store.
    #400  LoudnessReading.currentLimiter (the clip's own limiter as read, set at all four
          construction sites); solvedRow's keep rule (AU-64 (f)) compares the solve against
          it instead of the chosen default LimiterProps(). reading.limiter keeps its role
          in plan.
    #401  ProcessedLoudness.Key gains the document's recipeKey; key(clip:project:document:),
          Memo's lookup, LoudnessMeasureRun and AudioMatchRun pass it, so two open projects
          never share an R0.
    #413  AudioDynamicsLevels keys both memos by the plan text less every segment's
          `automation`, memoised per handle under the lock, so a Target or cap edit inside
          an action remakes no curve (AU-66 (e)); curveBuilds counts the clips whose curves
          were made.
    
    Spec index: audio.md 1703 lines, 11-decisions/ 24557 in 46 files (merged over b1's
    cells; spec_index_proof 276/276).
    
    Verified:
    - volume_line_proof.py --probe V1–V10 ok; red: --mutants M14 (rounding restored) →
      "M14 killed by V10 — failing rows: V10".
    - eq_probe.py Q1–Q12 ok; red: M12 empty-eq-counted → Q12 FAIL (eq {} read "0 on").
    - loudness_cache_probe.py C1–C13 ok; red: normalize-tip-unobserved (observer
      registration removed) → C13 FAIL (B's tooltip unchanged).
    - audio_ap6_probe.py E1–E12 ok; red: M13 keep-against-chosen → E11 FAIL (wrote 2.000,
      the keep rule fired on a clip with no limiter); M14 memo-without-document → E12 FAIL
      (the other document read this one's steps).
    - audio_ap6b_probe.py L1–L10, R1–R5 ok; red: M18 curves-keyed-by-plan → L10 FAIL
      (2 curves made across the Target edit).
    - make typecheck 0 errors, the 4 baseline warnings; spec_index_proof 276/276;
      docs_site_proof 0 problems.
    - make gate PASS on the lane's worktree (731 s) and on the integration worktree over
      main (578 s: names, typecheck, test, app; fmt and lint skipped as unchanged).
    - No MCP proof rows were added, so no Release proof run is owed.
    
    Owed: nothing.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

| **One per Track Name** | The mix, and one stem for each track name. |

The row sits under **Bit depth:**. On every format except the three audio-only ones it's greyed out and keeps your last choice.

The sheet remembers your choice with the rest of your last export, and a [preset](/export/presets/) stores it.

## Which tracks get a stem

Only tracks you can hear get a stem:

- A [muted track](/audio/mute-and-solo/) has no stem.
- While any track is soloed, only the soloed tracks have one.
- A track with no sound on it, only pictures or nothing, has none.

With **One per Track Name**, tracks whose names match share one file. The match ignores case and any spaces at either end, and the file is named the way the first of those tracks is spelled. A track with no name gets its own file. Name your tracks in [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/).

If no track can be heard, the sheet shows "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write", and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out.

## Stem file names

A stem is named after the mix and its track, and sits in the same folder. Exporting `Mix.wav` writes `Mix - Dialogue.wav` and `Mix - Music.wav`.

| Case | The stem's name |
| --- | --- |
| A track with no name | Its header's label: `Mix - Track 3.wav` |
| A `/` or `:` in a track name | Written as `-` |
| A name an earlier stem already has, ignoring case | Its track's label follows: `Mix - vo (Track 2).wav` |
| That name is taken too | A count follows the label: `Mix - vo (Track 2, 2).wav` |

No two stems share a file.

## Overwriting and clean-up

:::caution
An existing file at a stem's name is replaced without asking. The save panel asks only about the mix.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The acknowledgements (#376, spec §11 PUB-10): every third-party notice the bundle owes,
written each build into `Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt` by project.yml's "Write
Acknowledgements" step; byte-identical for identical inputs, written atomically.

    python3 tools/licenses/acknowledgements.py --out PATH [--strict-bun] [--sparkle-license PATH]
    python3 tools/licenses/acknowledgements.py --print-bun-version
    python3 tools/licenses/acknowledgements.py --selftest | --mutant dev-edges|nested-unchecked|bun-unchecked

Crates over every non-dev edge of `cargo metadata` (not FIRST_PARTY), npm from `agent/bun.lock`
(no dev dependency or optional peer), each with its root licence files, else `spdx/<id>.txt`
under its authors, NESTED deciding every nested licence file; then Bun (BUN_LICENSE_VERSION,
`--strict-bun` refusing another), Sparkle, the encoders, the model and the fonts. D42/D43
(dist_check.py) read the file with their own readers. The selftest is
`acknowledgements_selftest.py`; a `--mutant` fails exactly its rows: `dev-edges` G1,
`nested-unchecked` L3, `bun-unchecked` B1. Stdlib only, Python 3.9.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple, Optional

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
HERE = ROOT / "tools" / "licenses"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools" / "codecs"))
import build_codecs  # noqa: E402  (PINS: the encoders, in order)

FIRST_PARTY = ("framejob-core", "graphic", "framejob-mcp")
CARGO_ROOTS = ("core", "mcp-proxy")
TARGET = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
BUN_LICENSE_VERSION = "1.3.6"
LICENCE_PREFIXES = ("LICENSE", "LICENCE", "COPYING", "NOTICE", "UNLICENSE")
NESTED = {("rquickjs-sys", "quickjs/LICENSE"): True, ("rquickjs-sys", "vendor/wasi-libc/NOTICE.md"):
          False, ("fontdb", "tests/fonts/LICENSE.txt"): False,
          ("@anthropic-ai/sdk", "src/internal/qs/LICENSE.md"): True}
PATCHED = {"tiny-skia": "spec §11 PR-13"}
LIBRARY_LICENCES = {"svt-av1": "BSD-3-Clause-Clear (parts BSD-2-Clause), with the Alliance for "
                               "Open Media Patent License 1.0",
                    "libvpx": "BSD-3-Clause, with the WebM Project's patent grant"}
SPARKLE_LICENSE = Path("SourcePackages/artifacts/sparkle/Sparkle/LICENSE")
CRATES_IO = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
EXPECTED = {"dev-edges": {"G1"}, "nested-unchecked": {"L3"}, "bun-unchecked": {"B1"}}
MUTANT = None
PREAMBLE = ("Frame Job is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. It includes the "
            "third-party software below, each under the licence its entry names, followed by "
            "that licence's full text (or, where the same text appeared above, a pointer to it).")


class Entry(NamedTuple):
    kind: str
    name: str
    version: str
    licence: str
    source: str
    texts: tuple  # ((label, text), ...)


class Failed(RuntimeError):
    pass


def read(path):
    return Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def cargo_packages(metadata: dict) -> list:
    """Package dicts reachable from resolve.root over non-dev edges, FIRST_PARTY removed."""
    packages = {p["id"]: p for p in metadata["packages"]}
    nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in metadata["resolve"]["nodes"]}
    seen, stack = set(), [metadata["resolve"]["root"]]
    while stack:
        current = stack.pop()

# ---- the probe -------------------------------------------------------------------

def probe_rows(sources=ROOT / "app/Sources"):
    out = OUT / "probe"
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    entry = out / "main.swift"
    shutil.copyfile(HERE / "audio_ap10b_probe.swift", entry)
    binary = out / "audio-ap10b-probe"
    swift = sorted(str(p) for p in Path(sources).glob("*.swift") if p.name != "main.swift")
    found, problem = {}, ""
    try:
        if len(swift) < 100:
            raise swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed("app source set incomplete", [])
        swift_build.build(sources=swift + [str(entry)], output=binary)
        scratch = out / "scratch"
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
        scratch.mkdir(parents=True)
        result = subprocess.run([str(binary), str(scratch)], capture_output=True, text=True,
                                timeout=600, cwd=str(out))
        problem = result.stderr.strip()[-600:]
        for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
            parts = line.split(" ", 2)
            if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[0] in ("ok", "FAIL"):
                detail = parts[2][2:] if len(parts) > 2 and parts[2].startswith("— ") else ""
                found[parts[1]] = (parts[0] == "ok", detail)
    except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error:
        errors = [line for line in error.diagnostics if ": error:" in line]
        found = None
        problem = "swiftc: " + " | ".join((errors or list(error.diagnostics) or [str(error)])[:6])
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        problem = "the probe ran past 600 s and was killed"
    for name in PROBE_ROWS:
        if found is None:
            row(name, False, "the probe does not build: " + problem)
        elif name not in found:
            row(name, False, "the probe did not answer: " + problem)
        else:
            row(name, found[name][0], found[name][1])

input.content:
# Spec: stem names compared NFC-normalised and case-folded (fixes b4: #394)

## Goal
Two heard tracks whose trimmed names differ only in Unicode normalisation (e.g. "café" precomposed and decomposed) and/or case are one name to `core/src/export_stems.rs`: one stem in `names` mode, and the suffix rule in both modes, so no two stems write one APFS file. The owner chose the `unicode-normalization` crate (2026-11-09, option 1 on #394).

## Files
Work directly in the integration worktree `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-int` (branch `fixes-int`); paths below are relative to it.
- `core/Cargo.toml` — add `unicode-normalization = "0.1.24"` under `[dependencies]` with a one-line comment in the file's style (what it is for: `export_stems.rs`'s name comparison, spec §11 AU-108, #394).
- `core/Cargo.lock` — tracked (`git ls-files` lists it); gains `unicode-normalization` (its `tinyvec` dependency is already in the lock at 1.13.3 through `graphic`). Written by `cargo build`, never by hand.
- `core/src/export_stems.rs` — `same` compares the folded form; module doc lines 12–22 and `same`'s doc comment say "NFC-normalised, case-insensitively" where they now say "case-insensitively".
- `core/tests/export_stems.rs` — one new test (below); the module doc's "Pinned here" list gains the clause.
- `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` — AU-108 (b) and (c) amended in place.
- `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md` — AU-108's index row (line ~655) wording; `audio.md`'s Lines cell if its count moves.
- `designs/spec/07.8-export.md` — line ~511 "trimmed names match ignoring case" → "… match NFC-normalised, ignoring case"; line ~517 suffix clause likewise if it names the comparison.
- `designs/spec/07.10-rust-module-map.md` — the `export_stems.rs` row (line 142): "one per trimmed name ignoring case" → "one per trimmed name, NFC-normalised and ignoring case".
- `designs/spec/README.md` — Lines cells for any spec file above whose `wc -l` moved, and the `11-decisions/` folder cell (`N in 46 files`).
- `docs/site/src/content/docs/export/stems.mdx` — line 54's list of what the match ignores, and the suffix table's row "A name an earlier stem already has, ignoring case" (line 66), name the new equivalence in user words (no "NFC"): e.g. "…ignores case, any spaces at either end, and whether an accented letter such as é was typed as one character or as a letter and an accent".

## Interfaces
- `core/src/export_stems.rs`:
  - `use unicode_normalization::UnicodeNormalization;`
  - `fn fold(name: &str) -> String` (private) — `name` NFC-normalised (`.nfc().collect::<String>()`), then `.to_lowercase()`.
  - `fn same(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool` — unchanged signature; `fold(a) == fold(b)`.
  - `Stem { name: String, tracks: Vec<u32> }`, `Project::export_stems(&self, StemsMode) -> Result<Vec<Stem>, String>` — unchanged.
- No FFI, header, op, schema or format change; no `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` bump (nothing persisted changes).
- New test in `core/tests/export_stems.rs`, in the "grouping, order and names (AU-108)" section:
  `#[test] fn names_differing_only_in_unicode_normalisation_are_one_name()` using the existing `one_each`, `track`, `stems`, `named` helpers, with literals spelled by escape (`"caf\u{e9}"`, `"cafe\u{301}"`, `"CAFE\u{301}"`) so the bytes are visible:
  1. `names` mode on `audio_wav`: tracks `2 "caf\u{e9}"`, `3 "CAFE\u{301}"`, `4 "Music"` → `[("caf\u{e9}", [2, 3]), ("Music", [4])]` (grouped, named by the first's spelling — matches the existing case-equal rule in `names_mode_groups_case_insensitively_by_the_first_spelling`).
  2. `tracks` mode on `audio_wav`: tracks `2 "caf\u{e9}"`, `3 "cafe\u{301}"` → `[("caf\u{e9}", [2]), ("cafe\u{301} (Track 2)", [3])]` (the suffix rule, matching `a_name_an_earlier_stem_holds_gets_its_track_number`; the second keeps its own NFD spelling).

## Approach
1. Write the test first. Run `cd core && cargo test --release --test export_stems names_differing_only_in_unicode_normalisation` on the unfixed code; it must FAIL (names mode answers two stems; tracks mode answers no suffix). Record the failure output in `04-checks.txt`.
2. Add the dependency to `core/Cargo.toml`; the next `cargo build`/`cargo test` fetches it (network, once) and writes `core/Cargo.lock`.
3. Add `fold` and route `same` through it. Both call sites (`groups.iter_mut().find(… same(&g.spelling, trimmed))` and the `taken` closure `same(&s.name, name)`) are covered by `same`; touch neither.
4. Re-run the test: green. Then the mutant: restore `same` to `a.to_lowercase() == b.to_lowercase()`, run the test, record it red, revert. Record both in `04-checks.txt`.
5. Update the module docs in `export_stems.rs` and the test file's module doc.
6. Amend spec §11 AU-108 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md`: (b) "trimmed names match case-insensitively" → "trimmed names match once each is NFC-normalised and lowercased (so a precomposed and a decomposed spelling, which APFS stores as one file name, are one name; amended 2026-11-09, #394, the owner choosing the `unicode-normalization` crate)"; (c) "a name equal case-insensitively to an earlier stem's" → "a name equal to an earlier stem's under the same comparison". The stem keeps its first track's spelling as typed (not rewritten to NFC). Follow the in-place amendment style of #392/#407 in commit 448640ef. Update the AU-108 index row, §7.8 and §7.10 wording, then the Lines cells.
7. Edit `stems.mdx` as in **Files**.
8. Acknowledgements: `python3 tools/licenses/acknowledgements.py --selftest`, then generate once to the scratchpad (`--out <scratch>/fx-b4/Acknowledgements.txt`) and confirm `unicode-normalization` appears with its licence text; record in `04-checks.txt`. No change to `tools/licenses/` is expected; if the generator fails on the new crate, STOP and report (that file is not in **Files**).
9. `cargo fmt` in `core/`, `make lint`, targeted checks, then `make gate` once; commit (below).

## Constraints
- Only reader of `export_stems` is `core/src/export.rs:170` (`self.export_stems(mode)?`), which writes the settings' `stems`; its output shape is unchanged.
- The stem `name` is still the first track's trimmed spelling, verbatim (only `/` and `:` → `-`). Swift builds the file as `<mix> - <stem.name>.<ext>` (`app/Sources/ExportStems.swift` `url(for:mix:)`) and reports the path from the same string, so the file written and the result's path already agree; no Swift change.
- `ExportStemsPipeline.collision` (`app/Sources/ExportStems.swift:118`, AU-108 (d)) needs no change: it compares `String`s in a `Set<String>`, and Swift `String` equality and hashing are by canonical equivalence, so NFC and NFD paths already collide there.
- Existing tests in `core/tests/export_stems.rs` (case grouping, suffix and count rules) must stay green unchanged.
- Tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (core/CLAUDE.md "Tests"); no `#[cfg(test)]` in `src/`.
- File sizes: `export_stems.rs` 119 lines, `core/tests/export_stems.rs` 400 lines — both well under the ~600 cap for existing files.
- Never edit any `CLAUDE.md`; the edits owed are listed below.
- Commit on `fixes-int` naming paths explicitly (the files above, `core/Cargo.lock` included). Subject: what now works, ending "(fixes b4: #394)". Body: what changed; "Verified:" with the test seen red then green and the mutant red, lint, spec_index_proof, docs_site_proof, acknowledgements, gate; "Owed: nothing" unless something is; last line exactly `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The post-commit hook can take minutes; wait.
- Never push, never touch `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob` (main checkout), never open `.secrets/`.

## CLAUDE.md edits owed (the integrator applies)
- `core/CLAUDE.md`, "Dependencies" paragraph, append: "`unicode-normalization` (with `tinyvec`, already in the lock through `graphic`) for `export_stems.rs`'s name comparison only: stem names compare NFC-normalised and lowercased, because APFS treats NFC and NFD spellings as one file name (spec §11 AU-108, #394)."
- `core/CLAUDE.md`, the `export_stems.rs` map entry: "grouped per track or per trimmed name ignoring case" → "grouped per track or per trimmed name, NFC-normalised and ignoring case".

## Verification
